---
title: "Configuration reference"
---

<!-- Code generated by cmd/configdoc from the config package; DO NOT EDIT. Run `mise run generate`. -->

Every environment variable Sphericon reads, with its default and the rules its value must hold. A
value that breaks a rule stops the start with a message naming the variable.

The process environment wins over the `.env` files of a checkout, which are read in this order, a later
one overriding an earlier: `.env`, `.env.<SPHERICON_ENV>`, `.env.local`, `.env.<SPHERICON_ENV>.local`
(the `test` and `e2e` profiles read only their own `.env.<SPHERICON_ENV>`).

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Rules | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | — | required | yes | The PostgreSQL connection string, such as `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db?sslmode=require`; `sslmode=verify-full` with `sslrootcert` also verifies the server's certificate. The job queue LISTENs for new jobs on a session of its own: behind PgBouncer, it must reach Postgres directly or a pool in session mode, never transaction mode. |
| `PORT` | `3000` |  |  | The port the public HTTP server listens on, on every interface. |
| `SPHERICON_APP_URL` | `http://localhost:3000` |  |  | The public origin of the Instance, `https://` in production: sessions, mailed links and tracking and unsubscribe links are built on it, an `https://` origin makes the session cookie Secure, and its host is the Passkey relying party id (ADR 0052), so changing the host invalidates every registered Passkey. An Instance served on an IP address cannot use Passkeys. |
| `SPHERICON_MCP_URL` | — |  |  | The public origin of a dedicated MCP host, such as `https://mcp.example.com`: the MCP resource is then served there while the OAuth issuer and consent screen stay on `SPHERICON_APP_URL`. Empty serves MCP on `SPHERICON_APP_URL`. |
| `SPHERICON_TRACKER_URL` | — |  |  | The public origin the tracker snippet loads `/t.js` from and posts `/collect` to, such as `https://t.example.com`, when the tracker has a host of its own routed to the same Instance. Empty uses `SPHERICON_APP_URL`. |
| `SPHERICON_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` | — |  | yes | The token the external API's bootstrap operation takes in `X-Bootstrap-Token` to mint an API token of the oldest Workspace without a caller token. Empty refuses every bootstrap. |
| `SPHERICON_CORS_ORIGINS` | — |  |  | Comma- or space-separated origins allowed credentialed CORS on the cookie-authenticated surfaces (`/site`, `/staff`). Empty is same-origin only, which the bundled app needs; the bearer-token surfaces answer any origin without credentials either way. |
| `SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET` | — |  | yes | Signs sessions and mailed links. Outside development and test the start is refused when it is empty, shorter than 32 characters or a documented placeholder; generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`. |
| `SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET_SECONDARY` | — |  | yes | The second secret of a JWT secret rotation: accepted when a session or a mailed link is verified, never used to sign. It must differ from `SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET` and, outside development and test, holds the same rules. Empty outside a rotation. |
| `SPHERICON_SESSION_TTL` | `24h` | must be positive |  | The lifetime of a site session, a Go duration such as `12h`: both the token's expiry and the cookie's, with no refresh (ADR 0020). |
| `SPHERICON_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | — |  | yes | The base64 Tink keyset that encrypts stored provider credentials; the server does not start without one. Generate it with `sphericon genkey`. |
| `SPHERICON_LICENSE_KEY` | — |  | yes | The Enterprise Edition license key (ADR 0014), a JWT signed with Ed25519. Empty runs the open core. An expired key also runs the open core and logs a warning (ADR 0035); a malformed key or one whose signature does not verify stops the start. |
| `SPHERICON_SMTP_HOST` | — |  |  | The host of the SMTP relay the Instance's own mail goes through when `SPHERICON_SYSTEM_EMAIL_PROVIDER` is `smtp`. Empty leaves the Instance without outbound mail. |
| `SPHERICON_SMTP_PORT` | `1025` |  |  | The port of the SMTP relay. |
| `SPHERICON_SMTP_USER` | — |  |  | The user the SMTP relay is authenticated as; empty sends without authentication. |
| `SPHERICON_SMTP_PASS` | — |  | yes | The password of `SPHERICON_SMTP_USER`. |
| `SPHERICON_ACCOUNT_LINK_URL` | — | must be set together with `SPHERICON_ACCOUNT_LINK_SIGNING_KEY` |  | The address of an external account page. With `SPHERICON_ACCOUNT_LINK_SIGNING_KEY`, a Workspace Owner sees an Account link that opens it with a signed token. The app never calls this address. |
| `SPHERICON_ACCOUNT_LINK_SIGNING_KEY` | — | must be set together with `SPHERICON_ACCOUNT_LINK_URL` | yes | The base64 Ed25519 seed that signs the Account link token (`openssl rand -base64 32`). The matching public key is published at `/.well-known/jwks.json`, so the receiver needs no secret. |
| `SPHERICON_STAFF_JWT_SECRET` | — |  | yes | Signs the Staff member session and login challenge (ADR 0026, ADR 0063). Empty turns the Staff sign-in off; set, it must differ from `SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET`. The `staff` license feature and `SPHERICON_MODE=saas` require it. Generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`. |
| `SPHERICON_STAFF_SESSION_TTL` | `4h` | must be positive |  | The lifetime of a Staff member session, a Go duration: no refresh and no "remember me". |
| `SPHERICON_STAFF_HOLD_MAX_EXPIRY` | `720h` | must be positive |  | How far ahead a service may set a Staff hold's expiry, a Go duration; a later expiry is refused. |
| `SPHERICON_ABUSE_VOLUME_FLOOR` | `1000` | must be positive |  | The fewest sends in the trailing 24 hours, per Sending domain, for the abuse detector (`staff` license, ADR 0026) to judge its rates; below it nothing is warned or frozen. |
| `SPHERICON_ABUSE_WARN_COMPLAINT_PERCENT` | `0.1` | must be positive; must be below `SPHERICON_ABUSE_FREEZE_COMPLAINT_PERCENT` |  | The complaint rate, in percent, at which the abuse detector warns the Workspace's Owners by email, freezing nothing. |
| `SPHERICON_ABUSE_WARN_BOUNCE_PERCENT` | `5` | must be positive; must be below `SPHERICON_ABUSE_FREEZE_BOUNCE_PERCENT` |  | The bounce rate, in percent, at which the abuse detector warns the Workspace's Owners. |
| `SPHERICON_ABUSE_FREEZE_COMPLAINT_PERCENT` | `0.3` | must be at most 100 |  | The complaint rate, in percent, at which the abuse detector suspends the whole Workspace and tells its Owners. |
| `SPHERICON_ABUSE_FREEZE_BOUNCE_PERCENT` | `10` | must be at most 100 |  | The bounce rate, in percent, at which the abuse detector suspends the whole Workspace. |
| `SPHERICON_SUPPORT_EMAIL` | — |  |  | The support address shown to a Workspace's Owners with a suspension (banner and notice email), where they appeal. Empty shows none. |
| `SPHERICON_DB_AUTO_MIGRATE` | `false` |  |  | Applies the embedded migrations at start, convenient for a single replica. |
| `SPHERICON_DB_MIGRATE_TIMEOUT` | `10m` |  |  | With `SPHERICON_DB_AUTO_MIGRATE` on, the longest a start waits for the migration lock and the run before it fails, a Go duration; `0` is no limit. `sphericon migrate` has no limit. |
| `SPHERICON_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `1048576` | must be positive |  | The largest request body, in bytes, accepted on every surface but `/collect`; a larger one is answered `413`. |
| `SPHERICON_COLLECT_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `512000` | must be positive |  | The largest `/collect` batch (`POST /collect/events`), in bytes; a larger one is answered `413`. |
| `SPHERICON_COLLECT_MAX_EVENT_BYTES` | `32768` | must be positive |  | The largest single `/collect` event, in bytes: an identify body, or each event of a batch; a larger one is answered `413`. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_HUMAN_PER_MINUTE` | `60` | must not be negative |  | Requests per minute per client IP and endpoint on the public human-facing endpoints (signup, invitation accept, consent confirm); over it `429` with `Retry-After`. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_API_BURST_PER_SECOND` | `20` | must not be negative |  | Requests per second per Workspace on `/api` and `/mcp` (one shared budget); over it `429` with `Retry-After`. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_API_PER_MINUTE` | `600` | must not be negative |  | Requests per minute per Workspace on `/api` and `/mcp`, stacked on the burst limit. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_FAILED_AUTH_PER_MINUTE` | `30` | must not be negative |  | Failed credential checks (bearer token, collect key) per minute per client IP; successful ones are not counted. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_TRACKING_PER_MINUTE` | `600` | must not be negative |  | Opens and clicks recorded per minute per client IP. It never refuses a recipient: over it the redirect or pixel is still served and the event is not recorded. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_FAILURES` | `5` | must not be negative |  | Failed logins one account may have within 15 minutes before login answers `429` with an exponentially growing delay, even for a correct password (no lockout). |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_IP_PER_MINUTE` | `20` | must not be negative |  | Login requests per minute per client IP. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_COLLECT_PER_MINUTE` | `6000` | must not be negative |  | Requests per minute per Workspace on `/collect`, a budget of its own apart from `/api` and `/mcp`. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_COLLECT_IP_PER_MINUTE` | `300` | must not be negative |  | Requests per minute per client IP on `/collect`. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_SERVICE_PER_MINUTE` | `600` | must not be negative |  | Requests per minute per Service credential on the internal listener's service endpoints. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_FORGOT_PASSWORD_PER_ADDRESS_PER_HOUR` | `3` | must not be negative |  | Mails one address may be sent per hour by each of forgot-password, registration and an email-change request (ADR 0031). Over it the request is still answered `202` and nothing is sent, so the answer never tells whether the address has an account. |
| `SPHERICON_RATE_LIMIT_FORGOT_PASSWORD_IP_PER_HOUR` | `10` | must not be negative |  | Forgot-password requests per client IP per hour; over it `429`. |
| `SPHERICON_OUTBOX_RETENTION_FLOOR_DAYS` | `7` | must not be negative |  | The minimum age, in days, of a domain-event outbox row every consumer has processed before the prune job, which runs every 10 minutes, may delete it (ADR 0019). |
| `SPHERICON_EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS` | `400` | must not be negative |  | The age, in days, past which analytical Events are deleted by a daily job; `0` disables it (ADR 0019). Evidentiary Events (`marketing.confirmed`, `email.complained`, `email.unsubscribed`, a permanent `email.bounced`) are never deleted by age. |
| `SPHERICON_UNVERIFIED_USER_RETENTION_DAYS` | `7` | must not be negative |  | The age, in days, past which an Unverified User with no Membership is deleted by a daily job, freeing the address; `0` disables it (ADR 0030). |
| `SPHERICON_EVENT_LIVE_WINDOW_HOURS` | `72` | must be at least 1 |  | The age, in hours, past which the external API refuses a live Event as history that belongs in a Backfill. A Backfill and `/collect` are not limited. |
| `SPHERICON_TEST_INBOX_RETENTION_DAYS` | `7` | must be at least 1 |  | How many days a Test inbox keeps a Captured message (ADR 0058). |
| `SPHERICON_TEST_INBOX_MAX_MESSAGES` | `200` | must be at least 1 |  | How many Captured messages a Workspace's Test inbox keeps, the newest ones (ADR 0058). |
| `SPHERICON_DB_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` | `15` | must be positive |  | The most open connections of one replica's `database/sql` pool (ent, the event bus, job workers). The defaults fit two replicas under Postgres' `max_connections=100`. |
| `SPHERICON_DB_MAX_IDLE_CONNS` | — | must not be negative; must not be above `SPHERICON_DB_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` |  | The most idle connections that pool keeps. Empty is `SPHERICON_DB_MAX_OPEN_CONNS`. |
| `SPHERICON_DB_CONN_MAX_LIFETIME` | `30m` | must be positive |  | The longest a pooled connection lives, a Go duration. |
| `SPHERICON_RIVER_DB_MAX_CONNS` | `25` | must be positive |  | The most connections of the job queue's own pool (fetch, completion, leader election), plus one LISTEN connection outside it. Job workers use the `database/sql` pool, so it need not match their number. |
| `SPHERICON_SMTP_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS` | `false`; `true` in development and test |  |  | Lets a Workspace's SMTP Integration reach a loopback or private host on any port. Off, it may only reach a public host on port 25, 465, 587 or 2525. The Instance's own `SPHERICON_SMTP_HOST` is exempt. |
| `SPHERICON_OUTBOUND_ALLOW` | — |  |  | Comma-separated `host:port` pairs (a name or an IP address, one port each, no wildcards) that an outbound call to a third-party URL, such as a Webhook endpoint delivery, may reach although the address is private or loopback, such as `n8n:5678` (ADR 0039). Redirects are still never followed; a malformed value stops the start. Leave it empty on a multi-tenant host. |
| `SPHERICON_APP_LOCALE` | `en` |  |  | The Instance's language for the UI and its own mail. `en` is the only one; any other value becomes `en`. |
| `DO_NOT_TRACK` | — |  |  | `1` switches the Telemetry report off and locks the Owner's setting; it never switches the report on (ADR 0032). |
| `SPHERICON_MODE` | `selfhosted` |  |  | The kind of deployment, `selfhosted` or `saas` (ADR 0060): it alone decides the Release check, the Telemetry report, the email verification gate and the Sign-up survey. `saas` also requires `SPHERICON_STAFF_JWT_SECRET`, `SPHERICON_INTERNAL_ADDR`, `SPHERICON_TRACKING_CNAME_TARGET` and a system email provider. Any other value stops the start. |
| `SPHERICON_SENTRY_DSN` | — |  |  | The Sentry-compatible DSN the browser app reports its errors to, handed to the page when it is served. Empty leaves the browser reporting off. |
| `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | — |  |  | The OAuth client id of the Instance's Google Cloud app: with its secret, enables "Continue with Google" (ADR 0048). Register `<SPHERICON_APP_URL>/site/auth/signin/google/callback` as its redirect URI. One of the pair without the other stops the start. |
| `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | — |  | yes | The OAuth client secret that goes with `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`. |
| `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | — |  |  | The OAuth client id of the Instance's GitHub OAuth app: with its secret, enables "Continue with GitHub" (ADR 0048). Set `<SPHERICON_APP_URL>/site/auth/signin/github/callback` as its callback URL. One of the pair without the other stops the start. |
| `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | — |  | yes | The OAuth client secret that goes with `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`. |
| `SPHERICON_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` |  |  | The log level: `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`; anything else is `info`. |
| `SPHERICON_LOG_FORMAT` | `json`; `text` in development and test |  |  | The log format: `json`, or `text` for coloured human-readable lines. |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `sphericon` |  |  | The `service.name` reported on OpenTelemetry traces and metrics. |
| `SPHERICON_METRICS_ADDR` | — |  |  | The `host:port` of the opt-in Prometheus listener. Empty runs none; the public port never serves `/metrics` (ADR 0025). It must differ from `PORT`. |
| `SPHERICON_DNS_ADDR` | — |  |  | The `host:port` of a DNS server that verifies Sending domains and Join domains instead of the host's resolver, for a development stack that publishes its own records. Leave it empty in production. |
| `SPHERICON_INTERNAL_ADDR` | — |  |  | The `host:port` of the opt-in internal listener: the edge's on-demand TLS `ask` and, with the `staff` license, the service endpoints of the Staff surface (ADR 0026, ADR 0038). Empty runs none. It must differ from `PORT` and `SPHERICON_METRICS_ADDR`. |
| `SPHERICON_PRESETS_DIR` | — |  |  | A directory of custom Presets (ADR 0037): every `*.yaml` and `*.yml` file at its root loads beside the built-in ones at start, and a file that does not load, or reuses a built-in name, stops the start. Empty loads only the built-in Presets. |
| `SPHERICON_TRACKING_CNAME_TARGET` | — |  |  | The edge host a Workspace's Tracking domain (e.g. `t.example.com`) is a CNAME to, such as `edge.example.com` (ADR 0038, ADR 0071). Empty turns Tracking domains off: the section is hidden on Settings, Tracking and no host is set or checked. |
| `SPHERICON_TRACKING_HOST_HEADER` | — |  |  | The request header the edge sets to the customer's host, such as `X-Forwarded-Host` (ADR 0038), believed only from a peer inside `SPHERICON_TRACKING_EDGE_CIDRS`. Empty uses the connection's `Host`. Have the proxy of the Instance's own host drop this header. |
| `SPHERICON_TRACKING_EDGE_CIDRS` | `127.0.0.0/8,::1/128` |  |  | Comma- or space-separated CIDRs the edge connects from: the only peers whose `SPHERICON_TRACKING_HOST_HEADER` is believed. A proxy on another machine must be listed. |
| `SPHERICON_SYSTEM_EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `smtp` |  |  | The provider of the Instance's own mail (verification, password reset, invitations): `smtp`, through `SPHERICON_SMTP_HOST`, or `ses`, through the `SPHERICON_SES_*` credentials. |
| `SPHERICON_SYSTEM_EMAIL_FROM` | `noreply@sphericon.localhost` |  |  | The From of the Instance's own mail: a bare address or `Name <noreply@example.com>`. An invalid value stops the start. |
| `SPHERICON_SYSTEM_EMAIL_REPLY_TO` | — |  |  | One bare address, such as `replies@example.com`, put in the `Reply-To` of the Instance's own mail. Empty sets no header; an invalid value stops the start. |
| `SPHERICON_SES_REGION` | — |  |  | The region of the SES-compatible service of the `ses` provider. |
| `SPHERICON_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | — |  | yes | The access key id of the SES-compatible service of the `ses` provider. |
| `SPHERICON_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | — |  | yes | The secret access key of the SES-compatible service of the `ses` provider. |

## Variables read outside the configuration

| Variable | Default | Rules | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SPHERICON_ENV` | — |  |  | The profile the process runs under, read before anything else: it picks the `.env` files and the defaults that depend on it. `development` (also when empty), `test` and `e2e` tolerate a missing `SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET` and let a Workspace's SMTP Integration reach a private host; `development` and `test` log as text, and `e2e`, the end-to-end suite's profile, has no rate limits. Any other name is a production profile. The release image sets `production`. |
| `OTEL_CONFIG_FILE` | — |  |  | Path of an OpenTelemetry declarative configuration file (YAML), which says where traces, metrics and logs are exported. Unset, nothing is exported over OTLP. |

## Secrets from files

Docker and Kubernetes mount secrets as files. Each secret variable also accepts a `<NAME>_FILE` sibling (`SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET_FILE=/run/secrets/jwt`) whose value is the path of a file read at start; the trailing newline is trimmed. A value set directly wins and its file is never read; an unreadable or empty file stops the start, naming the `_FILE` variable. `sphericon doctor` redacts every secret value from what it prints. The secret variables:

- `DATABASE_URL`
- `SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET`
- `SPHERICON_JWT_SECRET_SECONDARY`
- `SPHERICON_STAFF_JWT_SECRET`
- `SPHERICON_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
- `SPHERICON_SMTP_PASS`
- `SPHERICON_LICENSE_KEY`
- `SPHERICON_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
- `SPHERICON_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
- `SPHERICON_ACCOUNT_LINK_SIGNING_KEY`
- `SPHERICON_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`
- `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`
- `SPHERICON_SIGNIN_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`
